title: The Premium Lines Counted When Cover Is Given Up
content:
What counts as the premium collected, when cover under the Travel Protection Plans is given up, is read off
the shape of the policy's own premium record: whether anything has already been returned on it, and whether a
line was charged for the issue fee.

## The three readings

1. Where the premium record carries a line already returned on the policy and a line charged for the issue fee,
   the premium the record shows collected is the lines charged and the re-ratings raised, less the lines already
   returned and less the issue fee.
2. Where the premium record carries a line charged for the issue fee and no line already returned, it is the
   lines charged and the re-ratings raised less the issue fee.
3. In every other case the premium the record shows collected is the whole of the lines charged and the
   re-ratings raised on the policy together with the lines already returned on it.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A premium record carrying charges of 680.00, of which 15.00 is the issue fee, a re-rating of 45.00 and a line
already returned of 120.00 falls under the first reading, and the premium collected is 590.00. The same record
without the returned line falls under the second, and the premium collected is 710.00. A record carrying no line
for the issue fee falls under the third whatever else it holds, and the premium collected is 605.00 where the
returned line stands and 725.00 where it does not. The figures are hypothetical.
